hook: A p38α-MK2 kinase pathway builds nuclear actin after chemo; blocking it sensitizes ovarian cancer cells.
hook_turn: blocking it sensitizes ovarian cancer cells.
summary: A deep learning tool, nFANet, counted nuclear F-actin and a kinome screen identified p38α MAPK as a regulator that acts through MK2 and formins. Inhibiting or knocking out the pathway made ovarian cancer cells more sensitive to platinum therapy. The work is in cell lines and models, so patient benefit is not shown.
title: The p38α MAPK-MK2 axis drives chemotherapy-mediated nuclear actin remodeling to promote ovarian cancer progression.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
